cancer_indication: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer in combination regimens (with capecitabine after progression on anthracycline, taxane, and trastuzumab therapy; or with letrozole in postmenopausal patients whose tumors co-express hormone receptors).
moa: Lapatinib is an oral small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor that reversibly inhibits EGFR (ERBB1) and HER2 (ERBB2) by binding the intracellular ATP-binding site, preventing autophosphorylation and downstream signaling. In HER2-driven breast cancer, this interrupts key oncogenic cascades including PI3K–AKT–mTOR and MAPK signaling, leading to G1 cell-cycle arrest and reduced proliferation, with apoptosis in some contexts. In ER+/HER2+ tumors, HER2 and estrogen receptor pathways can cross-talk, and HER2 blockade can shift reliance toward ER signaling, supporting combination with endocrine therapy.

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Growth factor receptor signaling through ERBB family receptors (including EGFR and HER2) that activates downstream MAPK and PI3K pathway outputs controlling proliferation and survival.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: ERBB signaling is a dominant oncogenic driver in HER2-amplified breast cancers and strongly influences tumor growth and therapeutic response to HER2-directed strategies.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: HER2-amplified/ERBB-driven breast cancers show high ERBB signaling “oncogene addiction,” making dual EGFR/HER2 TKI blockade effective.
PMID:17192538; NCT00078572; PMID:18283035; FDA label: TYKERB (lapatinib) NDA 022059; DrugBank:DB01259; ChEMBL:CHEMBL554; KEGG:hsa04012; MSigDB:KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ERBB signaling can be high yet ineffective inhibition occurs when downstream PI3K-pathway lesions (e.g., low PTEN/PIK3CA mutation) or bypass RTKs blunt dependence on ERBB kinase output.
PMID:29110152; PMID:17192538; PMID:24044505; Reactome: R-HSA-6806834 (bypass concept)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2-nonamplified tumors with meaningful EGFR dependency (subset TNBC/basal-like) could show ERBB pathway activity not captured as “Up” yet still respond to EGFR/HER2 inhibition.
PMID:18283035; DrugBank:DB01259; FDA label: NDA 022059
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If ERBB signaling is low (HER2− / EGFR-low), there is little target engagement and lapatinib has minimal activity in HER2-negative breast cancer.
PMID:18283035; FDA label: NDA 022059

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib directly inhibits EGFR/HER2 kinase activity, reducing ERBB pathway signaling and slowing tumor growth in HER2+ breast cancer.
PMID:17192538; FDA label: NDA 022059; DrugBank:DB01259
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Partial ERBB signaling reduction can occur, yet tumors persist via parallel drivers (PI3K lesions, MET/NRG1-HER3 axis) causing clinical resistance despite pathway “downshift.”

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: A true increase in functional ERBB kinase signaling is inconsistent with effective on-target EGFR/HER2 inhibition producing sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB01259; FDA label: NDA 022059
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (adaptive rebound): Non-responders can show ERBB network rebound (e.g., HER3 ligand-driven reactivation) that restores downstream signaling and resistance.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core survival and growth signaling axis involving PI3K activation, AKT signaling, and mTOR-driven translational and metabolic programs.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway is a major downstream effector of HER2 signaling in breast cancer and supports tumor cell survival, proliferation, and adaptation under targeted therapy pressure.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: When PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation is primarily ERBB2-driven (no strong downstream PI3K lesions), upstream HER2 blockade can collapse PI3K signaling and yield response.
PMID:17192538; DrugBank:DB01259; MSigDB:HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K-pathway activation via low PTEN and/or PIK3CA mutations predicts resistance to anti-HER2 therapy without chemotherapy, including lapatinib.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Tumors with modest PI3K signature but strong ERBB→MAPK dependence may still respond to lapatinib via ERBB blockade and proliferation arrest.
KEGG:hsa04012; PMID:17192538
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K signaling plus low ERBB dependence suggests alternative drivers; lapatinib is unlikely to be effective.
PMID:18283035; FDA label: NDA 022059

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In HER2-driven cells, lapatinib reduces downstream PI3K/AKT signaling, contributing to growth arrest and apoptosis.
PMID:17192538; PMID:17308062; DrugBank:DB01259
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Bulk PI3K signature may fall, yet resistant clones persist through pathway re-wiring (e.g., mTOR/RTK feedback or parallel survival programs).

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Sustained PI3K/AKT upregulation generally counteracts lapatinib’s intended downstream suppression in sensitive disease.
DrugBank:DB01259; FDA label: NDA 022059
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive signaling (HER3 ligands, IGF axis, MET) can re-activate PI3K/AKT/mTOR despite ERBB2 inhibition, driving resistance.
PMID:24044505; PMID:29110152; Reactome:R-HSA-6806834

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Transcriptional program driven by E2F factors that promotes DNA replication and S-phase entry, reflecting active G1/S cell-cycle progression.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: Elevated E2F-target activity marks proliferative breast cancer states and is tightly linked to growth control mechanisms that determine tumor expansion and treatment responsiveness.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Highly proliferative HER2-driven tumors (high E2F targets) are often susceptible to HER2 blockade–induced G1 arrest.
PMID:23907131; PMID:17192538; MSigDB:HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If E2F activation is driven by RB-pathway disruption or cyclin/CDK alterations independent of ERBB signaling, ERBB inhibition may not suppress proliferation.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2-driven tumors are not strongly cycling at sampling but remain ERBB2-addicted and can still respond to kinase blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low E2F/proliferation signatures can reflect alternative biology (quiescent, non-ERBB driven) with poor TKI responsiveness.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib induces p27-dependent G1 arrest and suppresses cell-cycle transcriptional programs including E2F targets in HER2+ breast cancer cells.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistant cells can show partial E2F suppression yet survive via anti-apoptotic or metabolic rewiring, yielding clinical resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Persistent/upregulated E2F targets imply continued proliferation, which contradicts lapatinib sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Acquired resistance can restore cell-cycle progression and E2F programs through bypass signaling and checkpoint escape.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Early transcriptional response program induced by estrogen receptor signaling that regulates hormone-responsive proliferation and survival genes.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation: Estrogen signaling is a key lineage driver in ER-positive breast cancer and can interact with HER2 signaling in ER+/HER2+ disease, shaping tumor biology and treatment outcomes.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (ER+/HER2+ context): In HR+/HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, ER pathway activity supports benefit from combined endocrine therapy + lapatinib.
PMID:19786658; NCT00073528; FDA label: NDA 022059; MSigDB:HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong ER transcriptional dominance with relatively lower HER2 dependence can reduce single-agent lapatinib efficacy (needs co-targeting with endocrine therapy).

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low ER signaling (often HER2-enriched biology) aligns with higher HER2 pathway dependence and better response to HER2 kinase inhibition.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If ER signaling is low because the tumor is also HER2-negative (immune/basal-like without EGFR dependence), lapatinib is unlikely to work.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (combination-dependent): HER2 blockade can shift tumors toward ER dependence; with concurrent endocrine therapy this adaptive ER “unmasking” can still yield sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive ER signaling can compensate for HER2 inhibition and drive resistance if ER is not simultaneously suppressed.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders, proliferation arrest and reduced growth-factor crosstalk can dampen ER-driven transcription in bulk tumor profiles.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: ER-response may fall yet tumors persist via non-ER, non-ERBB bypass programs (e.g., EMT/MET/PI3K lesions).

NAGASHIMA_NRG1_SIGNALING_UP.description: Signature reflecting neuregulin-1 (NRG1/heregulin) signaling activity, associated with HER3- and EGFR-linked downstream pathway activation.
NAGASHIMA_NRG1_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation: NRG1-driven signaling can provide growth-factor ligand input into ERBB network activity in breast cancer models, affecting pathway utilization and adaptive signaling states.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If heregulin/ERBB3 signaling is HER2-dependent (HER2-HER3 dimers), HER2 kinase inhibition can still collapse the axis and induce response.
Reactome:R-HSA-1306955 (ERBB2 complex context); MSigDB:NAGASHIMA_NRG1_SIGNALING_UP
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: A heregulin (NRG1)–EGFR/HER3 autocrine loop is a documented mechanism of acquired lapatinib resistance in HER2+ breast cancer models.
PMID:24044505; PMID:25691057; MSigDB:NAGASHIMA_NRG1_SIGNALING_UP

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low NRG1/HER3-ligand drive reduces a major bypass route, increasing reliance on HER2 kinase signaling and sensitivity to lapatinib.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even without NRG1 drive, resistance can arise via other bypass RTKs (e.g., MET) or downstream PI3K lesions.
PMID:29110152; Reactome:R-HSA-6806834

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Induction of NRG1/HER3-ligand programs after HER2 blockade generally reflects adaptive escape rather than sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib can select for/induce NRG1-HER3 signaling rebound that restores downstream PI3K/MAPK and drives resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders (or with HER3-ligand blockade combinations), NRG1/HER3-driven compensatory signaling is suppressed alongside ERBB kinase inhibition.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NRG1 programs may be low yet resistance persists via alternative bypass (MET/IGF) or intrinsic PI3K activation.

REACTOME_GRB7_EVENTS_IN_ERBB2_SIGNALING.description: Adaptor-mediated events in ERBB2 signaling involving GRB7, which can connect receptor signaling to downstream survival, migration, and focal adhesion-related programs.
REACTOME_GRB7_EVENTS_IN_ERBB2_SIGNALING.interpretation: GRB7 is co-expressed with HER2 in HER2-amplified contexts and participates in signaling architectures that support tumor cell behavior and pathway rewiring.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: GRB7 pathway activity tracks with ERBB2 amplicon signaling and contributes to proliferative ERBB2 signaling, supporting sensitivity to HER2 kinase inhibition.
Reactome:R-HSA-1306955; PMID:23593540; MSigDB:REACTOME_GRB7_EVENTS_IN_ERBB2_SIGNALING
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: GRB7-dependent signaling can persist in lapatinib-resistant models, implying adaptor-driven buffering or parallel RTK inputs to migration/survival.
PMID:26945445; PMID:31197024 (GRB7 in resistant lines, concept); Reactome:R-HSA-1306955

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2+ tumors may not show high GRB7 signature at sampling yet remain ERBB2-addicted and respond to lapatinib.
PMID:17192538; Reactome:R-HSA-1227986 context
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low GRB7/ERBB2-complex signaling suggests limited HER2 pathway engagement, reducing TKI benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: By inhibiting ERBB2 phosphorylation, lapatinib reduces GRB7 recruitment and downstream ERBB2 signaling output.
Reactome:R-HSA-1306955; DrugBank:DB01259
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: GRB7/ERBB2 signaling can drop yet resistance persists through downstream PI3K lesions or alternate RTKs maintaining growth.
PMID:29110152; Reactome:R-HSA-6806834

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increasing GRB7 events within ERBB2 signaling is inconsistent with effective HER2 kinase blockade yielding sensitivity.
Reactome:R-HSA-1306955; DrugBank:DB01259
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Pathway “up” after treatment can reflect ERBB network rebound/adaptive rephosphorylation that re-engages GRB7 and resistance.
PMID:24044505; Reactome:R-HSA-1306955

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: Cell-state transition program characterized by loss of epithelial features and gain of mesenchymal traits, associated with motility, invasion, and altered signaling dependencies.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation: EMT-like states in breast cancer are linked to invasive phenotypes and broad signaling changes that influence tumor progression and therapy response patterns.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Partial EMT states may still retain HER2 addiction; a subset can respond if ERBB2 remains the dominant driver.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: EMT programs can reduce ERBB2 dependence (including epigenetic HER2 silencing) and are linked to de novo resistance to trastuzumab/lapatinib in HER2+ breast cancer models.
PMID:34575017; PMID:26883193; MSigDB:HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: An epithelial state is consistent with strong RTK-driven proliferation and better response to HER2 kinase blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: EMT-low tumors can still resist via PI3K lesions or NRG1-HER3 adaptive signaling.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective HER2 inhibition can reduce invasion/survival signaling that sustains EMT-like programs, shifting toward a less mesenchymal profile.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: EMT signatures may decrease in bulk while resistant subclones persist through non-EMT bypass mechanisms.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: EMT induction generally correlates with reduced dependence on HER2 signaling and would not be expected in sensitive response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib can select for EMT-like resistant states (plasticity-driven escape), supporting resistance phenotypes.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_MET.description: Signaling downstream of the MET receptor tyrosine kinase (HGF receptor) that activates PI3K and MAPK pathways to promote survival, proliferation, and motility.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_MET.interpretation: MET signaling can function as an alternative receptor-driven growth pathway in breast cancer models and is relevant to tumor cell survival and invasive behavior.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: MET signaling can be present but non-essential; if ERBB2 remains dominant, lapatinib can still produce response.
PMID:17192538; Reactome:R-HSA-6806834
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (cross-cancer → breast-relevant): MET activation is a known bypass RTK route that can confer resistance to lapatinib-class ERBB inhibition.
PMID:22238368 (gastric; tag cross-cancer); PMID:26883193 (breast resistance pathways); Reactome:R-HSA-6806834

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low MET bypass signaling increases reliance on ERBB2 signaling, improving likelihood of response to lapatinib.
PMID:17192538; Reactome:R-HSA-6806834
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MET-low tumors may still be resistant via downstream PI3K lesions or NRG1-HER3 rebound.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Upregulated MET bypass signaling after ERBB inhibition is an escape pattern, not a sensitivity marker.
Reactome:R-HSA-6806834
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Adaptive MET/HGF signaling can restore downstream PI3K/MAPK survival signaling despite HER2 kinase inhibition, driving resistance.
PMID:22238368 (cross-cancer); PMID:26883193 (breast resistance pathways); Reactome:R-HSA-6806834

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In responders without MET bypass, MET signaling remains low (or falls secondarily), allowing sustained ERBB-pathway suppression to dominate.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MET can remain low yet resistance persists via PI3K lesions (PTEN/PIK3CA) or ER signaling escape in ER+/HER2+ disease.

REACTOME_FOXO_MEDIATED_TRANSCRIPTION.description: Transcriptional regulation mediated by FOXO family factors, typically activated when AKT activity is reduced, promoting cell-cycle inhibition and stress-response gene expression.
REACTOME_FOXO_MEDIATED_TRANSCRIPTION.interpretation: FOXO-mediated programs are part of tumor-suppressive and adaptive transcriptional responses in breast cancer, influencing cell-cycle control and lineage signaling interactions.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Higher FOXO transcriptional activity can reflect lower AKT suppression and intact tumor-suppressive stress responses that may synergize with HER2 blockade–induced arrest.
Reactome:R-HSA-9614085; PMID:23907131
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: FOXO programs can induce feedback upregulation of RTKs (e.g., IGF/ERBB3 axis) that buffers HER2 inhibition and promotes resistance.
PMID:33976188; Reactome:R-HSA-9614085

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: In HER2-driven tumors with high AKT, FOXO is functionally suppressed; lapatinib reduces AKT signaling allowing FOXO-mediated p27 induction and arrest.
PMID:23907131; Reactome:R-HSA-9614085
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If FOXO remains suppressed despite therapy (e.g., persistent PI3K activity), cells fail to engage FOXO-dependent arrest/apoptosis programs and resist.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib can activate FOXO transcriptional output (via AKT suppression), inducing p27 and pro-death/cell-cycle arrest genes contributing to response.
PMID:23907131; Reactome:R-HSA-9614085
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: FOXO activation can also drive adaptive RTK feedback (e.g., IGF axis) that restores survival signaling and supports acquired resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some responders may show lower FOXO signatures in bulk due to rapid tumor cell loss/contraction of transcriptional programs despite sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low FOXO output after treatment indicates failure to suppress AKT (or FOXO pathway impairment), aligning with resistance.
PMID:29110152; Reactome:R-HSA-9614085

BIOCARTA_G1_PATHWAY.description: G1-phase cell-cycle control pathway involving cyclins/CDKs and checkpoint regulators that govern progression toward S phase.
BIOCARTA_G1_PATHWAY.interpretation: G1 control is central to breast cancer proliferation biology, and shifts in G1 regulatory circuitry impact tumor growth dynamics and responses to growth-factor pathway perturbations.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Active G1/S machinery with HER2-driven proliferation is vulnerable to lapatinib-induced p27-mediated G1 arrest.
PMID:23907131; PMID:17192538; MSigDB:BIOCARTA_G1_PATHWAY
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If G1 progression is uncoupled from RTK control (e.g., CDK/p27-axis disruption), ERBB inhibition may not enforce durable arrest.
PMID:23907131; PMID:31720077 (review context)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Slow-cycling HER2-addicted tumor cells can still respond through survival-signal withdrawal and apoptosis induction.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low baseline cycling can reflect alternate dependencies where lapatinib-mediated G1 control provides limited benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib induces p27Kip1-dependent G1 arrest in HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells, suppressing G1 pathway activity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: G1 signatures may decrease, but resistant cells survive via compensatory survival programs (NFκB, metabolic shift) despite cytostasis.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Increased G1 pathway activity indicates continued proliferation, inconsistent with sensitivity to HER2 blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Resistant tumors can re-establish G1 progression after initial response via bypass signaling and cell-cycle escape.

HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION.description: Mitochondrial respiration and electron transport chain program supporting ATP production through oxidative metabolism.
HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION.interpretation: Oxidative phosphorylation reflects metabolic state and can be modulated during targeted therapy responses, contributing to tumor cell energetic adaptation in breast cancer models.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: OXPHOS-high tumors can still be HER2-addicted and respond to kinase blockade despite elevated mitochondrial programs.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Metabolic plasticity/OXPHOS reliance is associated with drug-tolerant states in breast cancer and can support resistance to targeted therapies.
PMID:39403185; DOI:10.3389/fcell.2022.717881 (OXPHOS in breast cancer); MSigDB:HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lower OXPHOS (often more glycolytic/high-growth phenotypes) can be more vulnerable to HER2 signal withdrawal and apoptosis.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: OXPHOS-low tumors may still resist via PI3K lesions or EMT programs independent of mitochondrial state.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (reported MOA feature): Lapatinib has been shown to enhance cellular respiration/mitochondrial function in HER2+ breast cancer cells, which can contribute to stress/ROS and anti-tumor effects.
PMID:39403185; MSigDB:HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Surviving persister cells can shift toward OXPHOS as an adaptive tolerance program, supporting resistance despite ERBB inhibition.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective growth arrest can reduce biosynthetic demand and mitochondrial pathway expression in bulk tumors responding to therapy.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: OXPHOS may fall, yet resistance persists via NFκB survival, EMT, or PI3K genetic activation.

HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.description: Inflammatory signaling program induced by TNF and mediated by NF-κB transcriptional activity, regulating cytokines and pro-survival responses.
HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.interpretation: NF-κB–linked inflammation pathways can influence tumor cell survival signaling and microenvironmental interactions, affecting breast cancer progression and stress responses.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In HER2-driven contexts where NFκB is downstream of HER2 signaling, tumors may still respond if lapatinib can suppress upstream HER2→NFκB activation.
PMID:23229346; PMID:17192538; MSigDB:HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline NFκB/TNF survival signaling supports anti-apoptotic programs and has been implicated in lapatinib resistance biology.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low NFκB pro-survival signaling reduces an escape route, facilitating lapatinib-induced apoptosis and growth arrest.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NFκB-low tumors may still resist via PI3K lesions (PTEN/PIK3CA) or NRG1-HER3 adaptive signaling.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib can inhibit NFκB activation in HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells via blocking PI3K/AKT→IκB signaling, supporting sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NFκB decreases, but resistance persists through other compensatory pathways (NRG1-HER3, MET, or intrinsic PI3K activation).

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Upregulating NFκB/TNF survival signaling typically antagonizes apoptosis and is inconsistent with a sensitive response pattern.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib-induced stress can activate NFκB in some settings and this adaptive survival response can underlie resistance; NFκB pathway increases are seen in resistance-associated contexts.
PMID:24216290; DOI:10.1186/s13058-021-01390-2 (RANK/NFκB after anti-HER2); MSigDB:HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB

BIOCARTA_PTEN_PATHWAY.description: Tumor suppressor pathway centered on PTEN-mediated negative regulation of PI3K signaling, limiting AKT pathway activation.
BIOCARTA_PTEN_PATHWAY.interpretation: PTEN status and PI3K negative regulation are important determinants of signaling balance in breast cancer and shape downstream survival pathway activity.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Intact PTEN pathway function constrains PI3K signaling and is associated with better response to upstream HER2 inhibition.
PMID:29110152; MSigDB:BIOCARTA_PTEN_PATHWAY
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Despite preserved PTEN function, resistance can arise through other bypass routes (NRG1-HER3, MET, EMT).

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: PTEN loss can still allow benefit when combined regimens (chemo/dual HER2 blockade) overcome partial TKI resistance; single-agent lapatinib benefit is typically reduced.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low PTEN and/or PIK3CA mutations (PI3K pathway activation) predict resistance to lapatinib-based anti-HER2 therapy without chemotherapy.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Lapatinib does not directly “upregulate PTEN pathway” in a durable genomic sense; any increase would be indirect and not a primary mechanistic effect.
DrugBank:DB01259; FDA label: NDA 022059
Resistance: Mechanistically not possible: Increased PTEN pathway activity would be expected to oppose PI3K survival signaling, not drive resistance to ERBB inhibition.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Post-treatment PTEN pathway loss reflects selection of resistant clones, not sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (selection): Therapy can enrich for PI3K-activated/PTEN-low resistant populations that maintain survival despite ERBB blockade.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Program encompassing intrinsic and extrinsic cell-death signaling, including caspase activation and regulation by BCL2-family proteins.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptosis competency influences whether breast cancer cells undergo cell death versus survival under therapeutic and signaling stress conditions.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline apoptotic priming increases likelihood of tumor cell death upon HER2/EGFR signal withdrawal by lapatinib.
PMID:17308062; PMID:17192538; MSigDB:HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis signatures can be present yet buffered by strong anti-apoptotic programs; resistance can still occur despite apparent priming.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even with low apoptosis baseline, strong on-target HER2 dependence can allow lapatinib to induce apoptosis after inhibition.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Poor apoptotic priming/blocked death pathways reduce lapatinib-induced killing and associate with resistance phenotypes.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lapatinib induces apoptosis in HER2-overexpressing breast cancer models (including trastuzumab-resistant derivatives), consistent with sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some resistant states show partial apoptosis induction but survive due to adaptation (e.g., anti-apoptotic buffering), motivating combination pro-death strategies.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In effective responders with rapid tumor clearance, bulk apoptosis gene expression can contract after initial killing despite overall sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to induce apoptosis after HER2/EGFR inhibition is a hallmark of resistance (often due to PI3K activation, NFκB survival, EMT, or bypass RTKs).

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Reported as upregulated in lapatinib-sensitive breast cancer cell lines and described as reinforcing RB-mediated G1 arrest and cell-cycle inhibition.
Described as upregulated and/or activated when PI3K–AKT signaling is inhibited, inducing anti-proliferative programs (including CDK inhibitors) in responsive contexts.
p27Kip1 is described as induced downstream of PI3K/AKT inhibition, contributing to G1 arrest in sensitive HER2-driven settings.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Low IGF1R activity is described as correlating with greater dependence on HER2 signaling and better susceptibility to HER2 pathway blockade.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Upregulation/activation of HER3 signaling is described as participating in adaptive ERBB network signaling that sustains downstream pathway activity despite HER2 inhibition.
Increased heregulin (NRG1) production is described as driving an autocrine signaling axis involving ERBB receptors that supports downstream signaling under HER2 inhibition pressure.
In ER+/HER2+ contexts, ER pathway reactivation/upregulation is described as an adaptive route that can maintain tumor cell growth when HER2 signaling is inhibited.
GRB7 is described as being induced as an adaptive response linked to ERBB2 signaling circuitry and associated with survival/migration signaling complexes.
AXL upregulation is described in EMT-associated states and linked to alternative RTK signaling that can maintain PI3K/MAPK outputs independent of HER2.
MET signaling is described as an alternative RTK pathway capable of supporting PI3K/MAPK activation and tumor cell survival when HER2 signaling is disrupted.
Activating alterations and hyperactivation of PI3K signaling through PIK3CA are described as enabling persistent AKT pathway activity that is less dependent on upstream HER2 input.
EGFR is a direct target of lapatinib and is also described as part of ERBB receptor signaling configurations that can contribute to adaptive ERBB network activity.
COX-2 (PTGS2) induction is described in an EGFR-positive TNBC model context alongside NF-κB activation and increased motility/metastasis-associated behavior.
Survivin (BIRC5) is described as part of anti-apoptotic signaling that remains elevated in resistant models, corresponding to failure to execute apoptosis.
BCL-2 is referenced as an anti-apoptotic factor within survival circuitry that can counteract apoptosis execution in resistant contexts.
BCL-XL (BCL2L1) is described as an anti-apoptotic factor that can blunt cell death pathways when survival signaling dominates.
MCL1 is referenced as an anti-apoptotic protein maintained by growth factor signaling outputs, contributing to reduced apoptosis when not suppressed.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss/downregulation of PTEN is described as removing negative regulation of PI3K signaling, enabling AKT pathway hyperactivity despite HER2 blockade.
Loss/inactivation of RB1 pathway enforcement is described as undermining the ability to enforce G1 arrest, allowing continued cycling under growth-factor pathway inhibition.
Downregulation or failure to induce p27Kip1 (CDKN1B) is described as reducing checkpoint enforcement of G1 arrest, weakening cytostatic effects.
Reduced expression of BIM (BCL2L11) is described as blunting intrinsic apoptosis execution, enabling survival under kinase pathway inhibition.
Loss of HER2 expression/amplification is described as eliminating the therapeutic target, resulting in lack of utility for continued HER2-directed inhibition.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive (HER2+) Breast Cancer: This is the primary subtype for lapatinib use. It includes HER2-enriched (ER/PR-negative, HER2+) and Luminal B HER2+ (ER/PR-positive, HER2+) tumors. Lapatinib significantly benefits HER2+ patients and is used in metastatic settings, including combinations such as lapatinib + capecitabine and lapatinib + letrozole.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B that are HER2-neg: Lapatinib is not used in these subtypes because the target (HER2) is not overexpressed. Clinical trials in unselected HER2-negative breast cancer were uniformly negative, and guidelines do not recommend lapatinib in HER2-negative disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): TNBC lacks ER, PR, and HER2; therefore, HER2-targeted drugs like lapatinib are generally ineffective. Although TNBC often overexpresses EGFR in basal-like cases, clinical trials of lapatinib in EGFR-positive TNBC showed minimal benefit and TNBC is not treated with lapatinib.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Low Breast Cancer: HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+ non-amplified) can benefit from antibody-drug conjugates, but lapatinib has no demonstrated benefit because HER2 is not overexpressed and the TKI does not have a strong target.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Brain Metastatic HER2+ Breast Cancer: Lapatinib can cross the blood–brain barrier to some extent and was used (usually with capecitabine) in HER2+ breast cancer with brain metastases, showing CNS responses in some patients, though newer agents have become preferred in many algorithms.
